headline: K-Map Router bypasses Google Maps limits in Korea with Naver/Kakao deep links & coordinate logic
summary: Google Maps is limited in Korea, making navigation difficult for visitors. A new open-source tool, K-Map Router, converts Google Maps links to Naver or KakaoMap routes, addressing complex deep linking and coordinate challenges.
details: Google Maps cannot provide walking or transit directions in Korea due to restricted map-data export. This forces visitors to manually copy and paste location names between Google Maps and local apps like Naver Map or KakaoMap.

K-Map Router is a free, open-source tool that streamlines this process. Users paste a Google Maps link, and the tool opens the location and route directly in Naver or KakaoMap, eliminating manual translation and searching.

The project, built with AI pair-programming, serves as a field guide to the undocumented complexities of Korean map deep links and coordinate systems. It aims to save developers time when building similar bridging solutions.

The router's backend uses a single Cloudflare Worker to serve both static assets and a POST API endpoint. Coordinate resolution is handled server-side to bypass browser CORS restrictions, using fetch, regex, and decoding without a database.

Parsing Google Maps URLs for coordinates is challenging due to multiple encoding shapes. Notably, /dir/ URLs store longitude before latitude, and mobile app links often contain base64url-encoded protobufs instead of plaintext coordinates.

The tool also addresses platform-specific quirks, such as Android's flaky custom schemes requiring intent:// URLs with store fallbacks, and Kakao's legacy desktop API needing conversion to its internal WCongnamul coordinates.

WCongnamul coordinates were found to be EPSG:5181 (a GRS80 Transverse Mercator) scaled by 2.5. The developer implemented this projection manually, matching Kakao's own conversions for various test points.

iOS clipboard integration presented unique challenges, including the need to make exactly one clipboard call inside a user gesture and then read the type from the already-resolved ClipboardItem to avoid permission issues.

The K-Map Router intelligently preserves the original Google Maps travel mode (e.g., driving directions) when opening routes in Naver or Kakao, allowing users to plan in Google Maps and navigate seamlessly in Korea.

headline_marked: [[VSCO launches Studio Pro]] mobile app, targeting pro photographers with $500/year subscription
headline: VSCO launches Studio Pro mobile app, targeting pro photographers with $500/year subscription
summary: The new app, rolling out today on iOS, aims to handle a professional photographer's entire business workflow. It will be part of the upcoming VSCO One subscription, priced at $500 annually.
details: VSCO has launched its new Studio Pro editing app, available today on iOS and coming to macOS later this year. The app initially offers tools for batch editing, style matching from a reference image, and sharing images through VSCO Galleries.
The app is designed for managing high-volume editing projects, catering to professional photographers working on weddings, portraits, events, sports, and other large-scale photoshoots.

Later this month, VSCO will introduce the VSCO One subscription bundle for $500 per year. This bundle aims to provide an alternative to using disconnected software platforms for photo editing and business operations, directly competing with offerings like Adobe Creative Cloud Pro.

The VSCO One subscription includes Studio Pro, Capture, Galleries, Workspace, Sites, AI Lab, Canvas, and a Freelance Photographer business mentorship program, offering a comprehensive suite for professional photographers.
Future updates for Studio Pro are planned to include support for RAW images, advanced export options, and additional advanced editing tools like adjusting image aspect ratios.
